newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to inspect Arkansas tornado damage.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to inspect Arkansas tornado damage.

text.p: President Bill Clinton travels to Arkansas on Tuesday to inspect the destruction from a series of killer tornadoes that struck his home state last weekend, leaving more than 20 people dead in their wake.

Clinton, a five-term Democratic governor of Arkansas, has already moved to make tornado victims eligible for federal disaster relief. He spoke to officials in the state soon after after the storms hit, and said people he knew were affected.
The twisters were the worst to hit Arkansas since 1968.
A White House spokesman said a federal action team already in place had assured the president "that nothing about his visit would complicate any ongoing recovery or disaster relief efforts."
"He'll be doing an aerial tour of damage," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

Clinton will begin his helicopter tour in Arkadelphia, a small college town about 50 miles (80 km) southwest of Little Rock that was one of the hardest-hit areas. He will later visit College Station just outside Little Rock.
The tornadoes destroyed or damaged hundreds of homes and buildings along a 250-mile (402 km) path from south Arkansas to the state's border with Missouri.
Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee, a Republican, called the destruction "apocalyptic" and asked the White House to declare eight counties disaster areas.

Clinton's trip forced him to reschedule a news conference that had been set for Tuesday. His question-and-answer session with reporters, which is expected to focus on the mushrooming campaign financing scandal, will now take place on Friday.
